_doc: LIVE-MCP scenario registry. Derived from marketplace_test_bank.json's journey lane by tools/build_live_mcp_registry.py - do not hand-edit the rows, edit the CATEGORIES table and regenerate. `status` moves owed -> walked -> green as the flywheel turns; findings accumulate per scenario so a re-walk can prove a fix rather than re-discover it.

categories.A-discovery: can a stranger FIND the thing they came for? (40% of simulated journey failures died here)
categories.B-listing-lifecycle: can a seller get a listing from nothing to live, and know why when they cannot?
categories.C-inquiry: can a buyer reach a human, and does the seller learn about it?
categories.D-service-hail: can a client raise a job and a provider take it, both knowing what state it is in?
categories.E-money: at the moment money moves, does every screen agree on the number?
categories.F-credits: does a person understand what credits are, what they hold, and what they will get back?
categories.G-trust: is a trust signal earned, visible, and impossible to mint for yourself?
categories.H-moderation: can an admin act, and is a non-admin visibly refused rather than silently ignored?
categories.I-map: does the map tell the truth about where someone is, and stay quiet when it should not?
categories.J-degraded: offline, slow, or failing: does the product REFUSE OUT LOUD instead of pretending?
categories.K-a11y: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, focus order - can this be used without a mouse or good eyes?
categories.L-comprehension: is the wording readable, translated, and free of jargon at the moment it costs money?
categories.M-mobile: at 390 CSS pixels, is every control reachable and every target big enough?
categories.N-continuity: does the page hold its shape while data arrives, and survive a reload mid-flow?
categories.O-empty-error: does an empty state promise only what the product can deliver?
categories.P-isolation: can one tenant see or touch another's rows, through any screen?

findings.title: the credits-back chip reads PHP500 on EVERY priced listing, so it stops informing
findings.measured: 9 of 18 cards carry a price; all 9 are PHP20,309-PHP236,110 and every chip reads PHP500.00. Each one AGREES with listing_reservation_amount() -- the per-listing cap is binding exactly as designed.
findings.why_it_matters: The cap was chosen from simulation for the PROVIDER side: it measured 4.9x throughput at scale, because a flat 10% locks PHP2,500 on a PHP25,000 listing and exhausts the supply. Nobody measured what it does to the BUYER side. On this catalogue the headline promise -- 10% back -- is worth 2.5% on the cheapest visible listing and 0.2% on the dearest, and the chip shows an identical number on both, so it can no longer help anyone choose.
findings.not_a_bug: The arithmetic is right and the guard is right. This is a DESIGN tension the simulation could not see, because it modelled provider throughput and not buyer comprehension.
options: state the RATE next to the amount ('PHP500 back - 0.2%'), so the cap is visible rather than disguised
raise reward_max_per_listing for industrial sections, where the current cap rounds the reward to noise
show the chip only when the reward is a meaningful fraction, and say nothing when it is not
findings.next: put this to Ian as an economy decision; do not silently change a simulated knob

findings.title: the filtered-empty state told people to 'clear the filters' and gave them nothing to press
findings.measured: Searching a term that matches nothing rendered 'No listings match those filters. Try a different search term or category, or clear the filters...' with ZERO buttons or links inside the grid. The only clear-ish control on the page was the 'All' category chip, measured 1,020px below the message, and it resets the CATEGORY while leaving the search term in place.
findings.why_it_matters: Discovery is 40% of simulated journey failures. This is the moment a stranger who mistyped decides whether the catalogue is empty or they made a mistake - and the single instruction on screen was not performable from where they were standing.
findings.fix: A 'Clear filters' button inside the empty state, delegated on document (the empty state re-renders on every load, so a boot-time binding would attach to a node that does not exist yet). Resets BOTH halves - category AND search term - because the message says 'the filters', and clearing half of what you promise is the same broken promise in a smaller box. Returns focus to the search box.
findings.verified_live: search 'zzzznothingmatchesthis' -> '' · cards 0 -> 9 · active chip -> 'All' · URL query cleared · focus back on #search-input · button 93x44px
findings.also_checked: Suspected the message sat below the fold; measured 341px between the search box and the message, so it is visible from where they typed. Not a fold problem - checked rather than assumed.

findings.measured: cold navigation as isidrosuarez: available PHP0, reserved PHP0, claim button visible. All four lifecycle states (draft/published/sold/removed) are named on the page, so a seller can see where a listing stands.
findings.nearly_filed: cw-total rendered EMPTY while the other two showed PHP0, which looks like a broken tile. It is deliberate - `total > 0 ? peso(total)+' total' : ''` - because 'PHP0 total' beside 'PHP0 available / PHP0 reserved' is noise. Reading the source settled it before it became a false finding.

findings.title: the account gate explained itself and then stranded the person
findings.measured: anon opens a PHP68,980 listing -> Contact Seller -> redirected to index.html?signin=1. The gate DOES toast a good reason ('Contacting a seller needs a WorkHive account, so they know who is asking. Joining is free.'), but nothing was stored: no ?return=, no wh_return_to, and index.html had no return handling at all. After signing in they landed on the homepage's marketing copy and had to find the listing again from scratch.
findings.why_it_matters: Discovery is 40% of simulated journey failures. This threw away the one visitor who had already survived discovery AND formed intent - the most expensive person on the site to lose.
findings.fix: marketplace stores the destination in sessionStorage before redirecting; index.html honours it after sign-in, scoped to same-origin /workhive/ paths because a destination read from storage is still untrusted input and an open redirect is how that becomes a phishing hop.
findings.second_half: The destination was only ever 'the marketplace', because the detail is a SHEET and opening one never changed the URL - a listing could not be shared, bookmarked or returned to at all. openDetailSheet now writes ?listing=<id> (replaceState, so Back still leaves the page), closeSheet drops it, and boot honours it after the listings arrive.
findings.verified_live: gate stores /workhive/marketplace.html?listing=<id>; a cold load of that URL opens the Honeywell listing; closing clears the param. 18/18 marketplace journey + discovery specs green.
findings.instrument_notes: Two false readings caught: querySelector('[role=dialog],.modal') returned the first CLOSED overlay rather than the open sheet, and the toast probe matched the provenance chip because it carries role=status. Scoped to .sheet.open and read the source instead.

findings.title: an anonymous visitor could TRUNCATE 140 tables - RLS is never consulted for TRUNCATE
findings.measured: as anon, rolled back: `truncate table public.marketplace_sellers cascade` SUCCEEDED, table read 0 rows. 140 tables anon-truncatable, 142 for authenticated, ~104,000 rows.
findings.why_gates_missed_it: validate_unprotected_write_grant requires RLS behind any write grant - correct for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, INERT for TRUNCATE. marketplace_sellers has RLS on and passed cleanly.
findings.fix: mig 20260803000028 revokes schema-wide + ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES; gate `no-client-truncate` locks it. storage.* TRACKED (postgres is not superuser and cannot assume supabase_storage_admin) and printed every run.
findings.found_via: G-trust walk -> badges all wrong -> read policy signed-in-only -> audit the writes

findings.title: every seller trust signal was invisible to anonymous visitors
findings.measured: Bryan Garcia is verified=true, sales=1 in the DB; anon saw verified=false, sales=0, tier=null. 0 Verified badges and 9 Bronze on the page, while the page's own source chip promises 'ID-verified sellers only in results'.
findings.cause: v_marketplace_listings_truth is security_invoker, so its join to marketplace_sellers runs as the caller, and mkt_sellers_read is USING (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL). COALESCE turned the NULLs into a confident false and a confident 0 - not an error, just plausible wrong signals.
findings.fix: anon row policy scoped to sellers WITH a published listing (not USING(true), which would have regressed the RLS ratchet), plus a column grant limited to the public signals after revoking the table-level SELECT - a column grant is a no-op while a table grant stands. The card now renders the STORED tier instead of recomputing 11/51 in JavaScript, which duplicated a per-hive knob.
findings.verified_live: verified badges 0 -> 3; 9 of 9 cards agree with the DB on tier and verification

findings.title: the credits explanation shipped in a title= only - invisible on touch, unreliable for a screen reader
findings.measured: chip had title= and NO aria-label (onlyTitle: true). There is no hover on a phone.
findings.why_it_matters: This chip was added TODAY specifically because 'credits unexplained' was 4.7% of all simulated journey failures. findings.fix: aria-label carries the sentence, role=note, title kept for hover, and the VISIBLE text keeps the fact ('PHP500.00 credits back') so no channel is load-bearing alone.
findings.verified_live: aria-label present and read back from the rendered chip; visible text still carries the amount

findings.title: 9 listing cards carried data-i="view" with no dictionary entry
findings.measured: 50 marked elements, 47 dictionary keys, 9 unresolved - all of them the card's primary action. An UNRESOLVED marker is a BROKEN translation, not a missing one: whI18nApply leaves the English in place while the page around it turns Filipino, so a Filipino reader gets a half-translated page and the one button they need stays in the other language.
findings.fix: added view: 'Tingnan' and clearfilters: 'I-clear ang filter' (the button added earlier in this same walk would have shipped with the identical defect).
findings.verified_live: with WH_LANG='fil': View -> Tingnan, and 0 marked elements remain untranslated
findings.instrument_note: The first check said the translation still did not land. That was the probe, not the page: whI18nApply returns early unless WH_LANG === 'fil', and the page was in English. Adding a key made the COUNT go green while proving nothing - the count is not the correctness.

findings.title: browser_resize(390) yields innerWidth 585 - every M-mobile scenario walked via MCP is a FALSE reading
findings.measured: browser_resize(390x844) then echoing innerWidth returned 585. A tap-target sweep at that width reported 0 violations, which says nothing about 390.
findings.why_it_matters: M-mobile is 12 of the 197 scenarios and its whole question is 'at 390 CSS pixels'. Walking them through an instrument that silently renders 585 would bank 12 green cells for a viewport nobody uses - the most expensive kind of pass, because it retires the question.
findings.resolution: M-mobile scenarios are walked through the PLAYWRIGHT SPEC lane (node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js), which sets the viewport deterministically - the marketplace-sim specs already assert 44px targets at a real 390. MCP keeps the categories where it is sound: content, wiring, oracles, a11y tree, and cross-persona reachability.
findings.rule: ECHO THE VIEWPORT INSIDE THE PAGE before trusting any width-dependent measurement.

findings.title: CLS 0.2302 - and 98% of it was blamed on decoration that cannot move
findings.measured: PerformanceObserver(layout-shift, buffered): CLS 0.2302 ('needs improvement'; good is <=0.1), with 0.2251 attributed to .aurora-blob a2/a3.
findings.diagnosis: Those blobs are absolutely positioned inside a `position: fixed; inset: 0` layer, so they cannot shift on their own - they were the visible VICTIM. The cause is the scrollbar: listings arrive, content (3345px) exceeds the viewport (1266px), a 23px scrollbar appears and the LAYOUT VIEWPORT narrows 585 -> 562, so every viewport-sized fixed layer re-lays-out. Confirmed by measuring innerWidth vs documentElement.clientWidth, not by reasoning.
findings.fix: html { scrollbar-gutter: stable } - canonical in components.css (18 pages), plus the 9 pages that carry the same fixed-full-bleed shape and do not link it.
findings.verified_live: marketplace 0.2302 -> 0.0423 (GOOD); marketplace-seller 0.1909 -> 0.0663 (GOOD). 13/13 specs across the four edited marketplace pages green.
findings.nearly_shipped_half: After the shared-stylesheet edit, marketplace-seller still reported gutter:'auto' - it does not link components.css. Measuring a SECOND page is what caught a platform-wide claim that had reached one page.

findings.title: a FAILED listings read renders an error, never the first-run invitation
findings.measured: fetch broken at the transport for listings only; 4 requests intercepted (the page RETRIES before declaring failure, so a short sleep would have measured the retry budget). Grid rendered "Couldn't load listings - Something went wrong reaching the marketplace. Check your connection and try again." with a Retry button and NO 'be the first to sell' CTA.
findings.why_it_matters: A failed read and an empty result are identical to a row count and opposite to a person: telling a seller 'be the first to sell' when the query merely failed reads as *your listings are gone*.

findings.title: the widened anon read is genuinely scoped, not a blanket open
findings.measured: anon sees 11 of 13 sellers; the 2 with no published listing (e.g. Jericho Bonifacio) return 0 rows. Private columns auth_uid and kyb_verified_at both refuse with 42501.
findings.why_checked: I had just widened this read myself. A fix that opens more than it claims is worse than the defect it replaced, so the scope was measured rather than asserted.
